title: CGM-derived glucose excursion phenotype as a cardiometabolic risk signal
topic_statement: Assess which glucose-excursion-derived phenotypes could support a defensible cardiometabolic risk signal, and lay out the trade-offs between candidate hypotheses before the group commits effort.

sections.title: Topic and scope
body: Research direction (fixed input): derive interpretable glucose-excursion phenotypes from continuous glucose monitoring and test whether they carry incremental cardiometabolic information beyond established summary metrics.

In scope: excursion detection and characterization from CGM-only input; within-person and between-person comparisons where the design supports them; explicit measurement validation before outcome association.
Out of scope: causal claims about diet or clinical events without reference labels; device-level algorithmic claims; and any advocation of a single direction.

list: Inferential boundary: an algorithm-defined excursion is not a meal, exposure, diagnosis, or response until reference evidence supports the attribution.
Access boundary: controlled-data analyses and external outreach are separate authorizations from this report.

sections.title: Evidence brief
body: Existing work establishes that CGM-derived variability summaries associate with cardiometabolic outcomes, while excursion-level phenotyping remains less standardized and largely unvalidated against reference labels.

list: Established: sensor-derived variability summaries and time-in-range metrics have reproducible associations with glycaemic control.
Contested: whether excursion shape and timing add information beyond those summaries, and how much of that signal is measurement artifact.
Gap: reference-labelled datasets that let an excursion detector be validated before it is used as a phenotype.

sections.title: Hypothesis portfolio
lead: Chip legend: Sci. risk = scientific risk, Exec. risk = execution risk, Time = time to evidence, Impact = potential impact. Scientific and execution risk read higher-is-riskier; time reads lower-is-faster; impact reads higher-is-better. The four axes stay separate and no composite score is computed.

body.title: Excursion timing carries incremental within-person information
body.claim: Excursion timing features predict next-window glycaemic state better than variability summaries alone.

scientific_risk.rationale: Within-person signal is plausible; confounding by sensor wear pattern is unresolved.

execution_risk.rationale: Uses existing CGM-only features and person-level splits.

time_to_evidence.rationale: Retrospective analysis on an existing cohort.

potential_impact.rationale: Methodological contribution to phenotyping; limited clinical reach alone.

body.prediction: Held-out within-person improvement over a variability-summary baseline.
body.falsifier: No held-out improvement beyond the baseline under a person-level split.
body.minimum_evidence: One existing CGM cohort with person-level splits and a frozen feature set.
body.rival: Wear-time and sensor-placement effects explain the apparent timing signal.
body.null: Excursion timing is redundant with existing variability summaries.
body.artifact: Detection thresholds, not physiology, generate the timing pattern.

body.title: Excursion phenotype is validated against reference-labelled excursions
body.claim: A detector validated against reference-labelled excursions supports a transferable phenotype across cohorts.

scientific_risk.rationale: Depends on reference labels that may not exist at usable scale.

execution_risk.rationale: Requires data access, labelling effort, and cross-cohort harmonization.

potential_impact.rationale: Would make downstream phenotype claims defensible.

body.prediction: Detector agreement with reference labels above a pre-registered threshold in an external cohort.
body.falsifier: Detector fails the pre-registered agreement threshold out of cohort.
body.minimum_evidence: One reference-labelled dataset plus one external cohort for transfer.
body.rival: Agreement reflects label construction rather than detector validity.
body.null: Detector performs no better than a threshold rule on the same labels.

body.title: Signal is explained by wear-time and device effects
body.claim: Apparent excursion-phenotype associations are attributable to wear-time and device differences.

execution_risk.rationale: Uses existing covariates and sensitivity analysis.

potential_impact.rationale: Protects every other claim from a common failure mode.

body.prediction: Adjusting for wear time and device materially attenuates the association.
body.falsifier: Association survives adjustment with a practically unchanged effect size.
body.minimum_evidence: Wear-time and device metadata in the same cohort.
body.rival: Not applicable — this is the rival explanation.
